children.text: Welcome to the second edition of Mathazine, “Mathematics for Plumheads”, our mathematics newsletter.

This edition explores the life and work of Al-Khwarizmi, the Father of Algebra, announces the Math Door Challenge for Grades 9–12, and explains dyscalculia and how it can affect everyday life. It also looks back at the soft launch event and includes a Sudoku puzzle, a comic, fun facts and math jokes.

children.text: Welcome to the sixth edition of Nawafidh (نوافذ), our Arabic magazine, which brings together our school’s events and our students’ creativity.

This edition covers September and October, including the visit of Her Excellency Dr. Aysha Al Sayyar, the International Day of Peace, Career Day, our sports achievements and the recognition received by our Arabic Language Department.
It also features students’ poems and stories, the Arabic language competitions for 2026–2027, pages on health, culture and science, and games and puzzles.

children.text: Welcome to the first issue of SAIS Times: “Empowering education with inspiration, innovation, and technology”.

This issue introduces Education 33, Dubai’s strategy to transform education by 2033, celebrates our PISA results and our teams’ success at the Curtin Sports Fest 2026, and looks back at the visit of Her Excellency Dr. Aysha Al Sayyar, who introduced her book Sirat Hayat, Sirat Watan.
It also covers our anti-vaping campaign, Teacher Appreciation, Peace Day, Breast Cancer Awareness Day, Ozone Day, the Book Fair, World Heart Day and Mental Health Day.

children.text: Welcome to the first edition of Well-being & Awareness for 2026–2027, a partnership with parents from our Student Support Services & Pastoral Department. This month’s focus is cultivating a positive mindset for the new academic year.

This bulletin is designed to be more than a source of information. It is intended to strengthen the connection between home and school by sharing practical guidance, well-being updates, important reminders, and strategies that families can reinforce at home.

We encourage you not only to read and discuss the information shared in each edition, but also to maintain two-way communication with our Student Support Services and Pastoral Teams. If you have concerns, observations, questions, or information that may help us better understand and support your child, we welcome you to reach out.
